newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf says Berre cuts not sufficient.
newsitem.headline: Elf says Berre cuts not sufficient.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine chairman Philippe Jaffre said that a capacity reduction at the Berre refinery in south France by Shell would not be enough to attack overcapacity in Europe.

"I fear that the the capacity reduction by Shell at Berre will not be sufficient. It could perhaps improve the local situation, but it will not significantly reduce European overcapacity," Jaffre said in an interview with the "Investir" weekly to appear on Saturday.
"Only the big refiners in Europe, Exxon, BP, Mobil and Shell can, by their decisions, pull up the industry," he said.
Jaffre said Elf was not closing any refineries. "In any case we have no intention of closing our refineries. They are modern, generate a positive cashflow and only need small investments," he said.
Elf's restructuring plan was aimed at returning to break-even in French refining and distribution in 1998, after 10 years of losses, he said.

Shell on February 8 announced plans to reduce capacity at its 127,000 bpd Berre refinery and sought formal approval to reduce crude throughput to 3.5 million tonnes per year from 6.5 million and shut one of its two catcrackers.
The Industry Ministry has so far not allowed a capacity reduction, preferring the oil companies to find a more wide-ranging plan.
Jaffre said in the interview that it was unlikely that Brent prices would remain at current levels.

"The most widespread assumption is that the crude price will slip until the autumn to about $18 (per barrel). The basic assumption for our investments is a medium-term price of $16.5. That is a very conservative level," he said.
